h1:
Koh Phangan 4 Days 3 Nights
Party, Quiet, Diving, Wellness
intro: Koh Phangan packs several personalities into one island — Haad Rin with its famous Full Moon Party, a quiet north with clear water, the reefs around Koh Ma, and Sri Thanu, the island's yoga and wellness capital. This 4-day 3-night plan fits all of it in, starting with the most high-energy day and winding down to an easy day of rest before you leave, with real prices and real spots that are still open.

blocks.html: What makes Koh Phangan special is how flexible it is. You can come to party all night, or come to find a quiet corner and fall asleep to the waves — all on the same island. This plan is built for travelers who want a taste of everything, and 4 days 3 nights is just about the right amount: not so rushed that you burn out, but enough to see the lively south, the calm north, and the wellness zone on the west coast.

Most trips start at Thong Sala pier, which is the main port, the market, and the hub of the island all in one. From there you fan out to each zone. Distances on the island aren't long, but some stretches of road are steep and full of sharp bends — and that really matters when you're planning how to get around.

blocks.text: Before you go — getting there and where to stay

blocks.html: Koh Phangan still has no airport, so you'll need to take a boat from Surat Thani or Koh Samui. The Lomprayah high-speed catamaran from Surat Thani runs around 350–450 THB per leg (transfers included in the package), while the Raja Ferry from Don Sak is cheaper at around 200 THB but takes longer, roughly 3 hours. If you're coming from Samui, the crossing is only 30–45 minutes.

items: Pick your base by style — party people go for Haad Rin (Haad Rin), chill travelers pick the west coast around Ban Tai and Sri Thanu, and those after real quiet head north to Thong Nai Pan and Chaloklum.
Rent a motorbike — from around 200 THB/day, available near the pier. It's the most flexible way to get around the island.
Songthaew (shared pickup truck) — runs the main routes between Thong Sala, Haad Rin, Chaloklum, and Thong Nai Pan. Good if you'd rather not drive yourself.
Taxis on the island have fairly fixed, high fares and are hard to haggle down — always write down the price before you get in.

blocks.title: On road safety
blocks.html: The roads toward Thong Nai Pan and some spots in the north are steep and get very slippery in the rain. If you've never ridden a motorbike on steep roads before, don't push it — take a songthaew or taxi, it's safer. Motorbike accidents are common on this island. Wear a helmet every time.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Arrival, Thong Sala, and the party south

items.activity: Arrive at Thong Sala pier, check in, rent a motorbike or arrange a ride
items.note: If you're coming for a Full Moon night, Haad Rin accommodation fills up and prices jump several times over — book weeks ahead.

items.activity: Wander Thong Sala market and try local eats at Phantip Night Market
items.note: Lots of variety — grilled fish, curries, fruit, all wallet-friendly. Opens early evening into the night.

items.activity: Catch the sunset on the beach at Beachlounge Thong Sala, with Koh Samui across the water
items.note: Beachfront bar, fresh seafood, good cocktails — a relaxed way to ease into the evening.

items.activity: Ride over to Haad Rin and explore the beach bars and nightlife
items.note: Even when it isn't a Full Moon night, Haad Rin still has bars open and Half Moon / Jungle Party events on some nights.

items.activity: If it's a Full Moon night, head into Haad Rin in the evening — music starts around 7 pm and peaks after midnight
items.note: Beach entry is 200 THB, paid at the gate; you get a glow-in-the-dark wristband.

blocks.title: Party smart
blocks.html: The Full Moon Party is genuinely fun, but the "buckets" (mixed spirits in a small pail) hit harder than you'd think. Alternate with plain water, never leave your drink and come back to it, always wear shoes because there's broken glass in the sand, lock your passport in the hotel safe, carry only the cash you need, and arrange your ride back in advance. Don't ride a motorbike drunk.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Snorkeling Koh Ma, Mae Haad, and the west coast

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Koh Ma snorkeling · Mae Haad · west coast

items.activity: Ride north-west to Mae Haad (Mae Haad), the island's best snorkeling spot
items.note: From March to May the tide drops far enough to expose a sandbar around 200 m long, and you can simply walk across to Koh Ma.

items.activity: Snorkel around Koh Ma (Koh Ma) and see the healthiest reef on the island
items.note: Shallow and fairly calm water — good for beginners. You can rent gear near the beach.

items.activity: Stop for lunch at a beachfront spot around Mae Haad–Ban Tai
items.note: Plenty of seafood places and vegetarian spots to choose from in this area.

items.activity: Continue to a quiet west-coast beach like Sri Thanu (Sri Thanu) and settle in for sunset
items.note: The west coast has the island's best sunset views — calm water and a laid-back vibe.

items.activity: Dinner around Sri Thanu — there are plenty of cafés and health-food spots to try here
items.note: A warm-up before tomorrow's wellness day.

blocks.html: If you want deeper diving or to go further afield, there are boat tours from Koh Phangan out to Sail Rock (Sail Rock), one of the Gulf of Thailand's famous dive sites, plus tours to Koh Nang Yuan and Koh Tao. Full-day tours start around 1,800–2,200 THB per person (roughly USD 58–66) and usually include hotel transfers, lunch, gear, and a guide.

blocks.title: Sea safety
blocks.html: Always check the surf and currents before you get in, especially if you're not a strong swimmer. Wear a life jacket on boat tours, don't touch or step on the coral, and use reef-safe sunscreen to help protect the reefs.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Quiet north, waterfalls, and viewpoints

items.activity: Ride north to Chaloklum (Chaloklum), a quiet, peaceful fishing village
items.note: It's the launch point for Bottle Beach (Bottle Beach).

items.activity: Take a longtail boat from Chaloklum to Bottle Beach, a quiet beach reached mainly by boat
items.note: Negotiate the round-trip boat fare at the pier. Go in the morning and come back in the afternoon for an easy half day.

items.activity: Head back to Chaloklum for lunch — fresh, well-priced seafood
items.note: Chaloklum is known for seafood, since it's a fishing village.

items.activity: Visit Phaeng Waterfall (Phaeng Waterfall) and hike up to Domsila Viewpoint
items.note: The climb is tiring but gives you a full panorama of the island. Wear shoes with good grip.

items.activity: Stop by Thong Nai Pan (Thong Nai Pan) in the northeast — clear water and a beautiful beach
items.note: This stretch of road is very steep; drive slowly, or take a songthaew if you're not confident.

blocks.html: Beyond Phaeng Waterfall, Koh Phangan has other falls worth a stop along the way, like Than Sadet Waterfall in the national park (with an easy enough trail to reach it) and Paradise Waterfall, if you have time to spare and love nature.

blocks.text: Day 4 — A wellness day in Sri Thanu before heading home

items.activity: Join a morning yoga class in Sri Thanu (Sri Thanu), the island's wellness hub
items.note: Centers like Orion Healing, Ananda Yoga, and Wonderland have daily drop-in classes.

items.activity: Healthy breakfast at a raw-food café or smoothie-bowl spot in Sri Thanu
items.note: This area has the island's densest concentration of vegetarian cafés and herbal juice bars.

items.activity: Pack up, return the motorbike, and pick up souvenirs at Thong Sala market
items.note: Allow at least 30–45 minutes to reach the pier before your boat departs.

items.activity: Take the boat back to Surat Thani / Don Sak, or to Samui to catch a flight
items.note: Check boat times ahead — late-afternoon departures can be limited in some seasons.

blocks.html: If you want to get serious about wellness, many centers in Sri Thanu run 3–14 day detox and yoga programs, starting around 13,000–14,000 THB per week (roughly USD 400–420) for a shared room, including yoga and meditation classes plus three plant-based meals a day. Private sea-view bungalows cost more. If this is your thing, you might extend the trip beyond 4 days.

items: Round-trip boat — around 700–900 THB (from Surat Thani, return)
3 nights' accommodation — guesthouse/bungalow around 1,500–4,500 THB (swings with the season and Full Moon nights — to be honest, Full Moon nights are much more expensive)
Motorbike rental for 3 days — around 600 THB plus fuel
1-day diving tour — around 1,800–2,200 THB (if you choose a boat tour)
Food/drinks — around 1,500–3,000 THB for the whole trip, depending on how you eat
Full Moon Party entry — 200 THB (Full Moon nights only)

blocks.html: All in, a budget version of this trip runs around 6,000–8,000 THB per person, and goes up depending on the accommodation and tours you pick. Room rates on the island swing a lot with the season — high season (December to April) and Full Moon nights are the priciest.

blocks.text: Food you shouldn't miss on the island

items.name: Phantip Night Market, Thong Sala
items.blurb: A night market in the heart of Thong Sala with dozens of local food stalls — grilled fish, southern curries, meatballs, fruit, sweets. The best place to start eating cheap and well on the island.
items.meta: Night market · Thong Sala · ฿60–150 a dish

items.name: Beachlounge Thong Sala
items.blurb: A beachfront bar-restaurant in Thong Sala looking out at Koh Samui across the water, with fresh seafood, Asian fusion, and a solid cocktail and wine list. Great for a sunset dinner.

items.name: Seafood spots at Chaloklum Bay
items.blurb: Chaloklum is a fishing village in the north, and the seafood here is fresher and better-priced than in the tourist zones. A good lunch stop on the day you head north.

items.name: Health cafés in Sri Thanu
items.blurb: Sri Thanu has the island's densest cluster of vegetarian cafés, raw food, smoothie bowls, and herbal juices. Perfect for breakfast on your wellness day.

items.name: Ando Loco
items.blurb: A budget-friendly Mexican spot with burritos, tacos, and vegetarian options. Laid-back vibe — good for a casual dinner with a group of friends.

items.name: The Masons Arms
items.blurb: A proper English pub about 2.5 km north of Thong Sala pier, with a full pub menu, English beers on tap, an upstairs balcony, and a beer garden. Good for a chill night out without the heavy party scene.

faq.q: Is 4 days 3 nights enough for Koh Phangan?
faq.a: It's enough to hit all the highlights — the party south, snorkeling at Koh Ma, the quiet north, and a wellness day in Sri Thanu. If you want to commit to a serious detox-yoga program, or take a slower pace, allow 5–6 days.

faq.q: Do you have to go on a Full Moon night to make it worth it?
faq.a: Not at all. Koh Phangan is fun any night — Haad Rin has bars open and events like Half Moon / Jungle Party on other nights too. The upside of skipping the Full Moon is cheaper accommodation and a less crowded island. For reference, Full Moon nights in 2026 fall around 31 May, 29 Jun, 29 Jul, 28 Aug and so on — check the date before you book.

faq.q: Is accommodation on Koh Phangan expensive?
faq.a: Prices swing a lot with season and location. Guesthouses start at just a few hundred baht, but in high season and on Full Moon nights they climb several times over, especially in Haad Rin. Book weeks ahead if you're going for a Full Moon night.

faq.q: Can you get around Koh Phangan without riding a motorbike?
faq.a: Yes. Songthaews run the main routes, and there are island taxis (fares are fairly fixed and high, hard to haggle). Some northern roads are steep and slippery — if you're not used to riding on steep roads, a songthaew or a chartered ride is safer.

faq.q: When is the best time to visit Koh Phangan?
faq.a: Roughly May to October the sea is clear and great for swimming and snorkeling, while from March to May the tide drops enough to form a sandbar you can walk across to Koh Ma. That said, island weather can be unpredictable — always check the forecast before you go.
